Quia virtutem Tuam non dileximus, nec

main_text.l: Ne tibi parvæ videantur quas Ego & Re-
gna mea ærumnas pertulimus, sed peccata nos-
tra reddas conscientiis nostris qualia in speculo
Iudiciorum Tuorum exhibentur, conspicua : haud
enim parva delicta tam atrociter soles casti-
gare.
O ergo pro magnarum Tuarum Misericor-
diarum multitudine, ignosce peccatis nostris, &
Iudicia Tua removeas vehementer multa, &
gravia.
Premant tamen Nos usque peccata nostra,
grauius faxis quam Iudicia, fac nos magis in
refipiscentiam, quam in liberationem gestire ; Da
nobis inprimis pœnitentis Conscientiæ pacem, &
tranquillitatem deinde in Conjunctione Regno-
rum.
In seruatoris nostri sanguinis Mari, obruas
precor peccata nostra, & per Rubrum hoc no-
stri sanguinis Mare, ad stationem aliquam Pie-
tatis, Pacis, Affluentiæ perducas.
Vt pro Publico Meo Munere, quo omnes
contingo, Populi mei perpessionibus confocior, itæ

page.notes: The first line is a fragment at the page head ("stianis" for Christianis) and is kept as printed. The catchword "faxis" stands at the lower right, below the last line. The line "Vt pro Publico..." is set in ordinary type; "itæ" is the last word of the text. Long s is given as plain s throughout. The Greek running head is given in Greek letters as printed. No printed errors were corrected.
